reason: Radioactive heating is the chapter’s stated mechanism for changing young bodies’ interiors, so I’ll start with a rocky planetesimal.
expectation: The heating should warm or melt a rocky body, beginning the separation of its materials.

effect: The rocky planetesimal has melted, making gravity-driven separation a plausible next step.
reaction: The distinction that not all asteroids melt is useful.
reason: Gravity can separate dense metal from lighter rock inside a molten body.
expectation: The body should differentiate into metal-rich and rocky layers.

effect: Gravity separated metal from silicate, producing a differentiated small world.
reaction: It is interesting that differentiation can happen before Earth finishes growing.
reason: Collisions could break the differentiated body and expose its stone and metal.

choice.combine: A small world with a metal core

expectation: The collision should expose fragments from the body's rocky and metallic layers.

effect: The collision exposed metal from the core; the goal may also require rocky fragments.
reaction: The link to iron meteorites is interesting.
reason: Heating the icy planetesimals should begin the other goal's route toward water-altered rock.
expectation: Radioactive heating should melt some ice within an icy body.

alternatives.reason: I could check whether the core fragments have a further role in exposing stone and metal.

effect: Internal heating produced liquid water confined within the icy body, ready to interact with rock.
reaction: The possibility of liquid water beneath a frozen exterior is interesting.
reason: Water reacting with silicate grains is a plausible way to form water-altered rock.

choice.combine: Liquid water inside an icy body

expectation: The water and silicates should form hydrated minerals that retain water in rock.

effect: Water reacting with silicates produced hydrated asteroid rock and completed the water-retention goal.
reaction: It is useful to see how hydrogen can remain in rock after exposed ice is gone.
reason: The remaining goal also mentions stone, so I’ll check what further collisions can expose.
expectation: The compatibility report may identify a body that can yield rocky fragments.

effect: Collisions currently have no available operations, so another route must complete the remaining goal.
reaction: That is surprising after the collision exposed the core.
reason: The exposed core fragments may have a remaining partner that reveals how to complete the stone-and-metal goal.
expectation: The compatibility report may identify the material needed to complete the goal.

effect: The core fragments have no available operation, so the remaining goal likely needs another material.
reaction: I’m unsure how to expose the stone after the collision.
reason: The differentiated world may have another available operation that produces rocky material.

choice.inspect: A small world with a metal core

expectation: Its compatibility report may reveal a way to expose stone.

effect: The differentiated body cooled and solidified, revealing a likely route to exposing its rocky exterior.
reaction: Cooling before exposing the stone makes sense.
reason: A collision may break the cooled asteroid and expose its rocky material.
expectation: The collision should expose rocky fragments from the asteroid's exterior.

effect: The collision exposed the cooled asteroid’s rocky layers and completed the remaining goal, alongside the previously exposed core fragments.
reaction: It was satisfying to finish both sides of the differentiated body’s story.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making water-bearing asteroid rock showed how water–rock reactions can retain hydrogen even after exposed ice is gone, a useful connection to Earth’s volatile inventory.

leastWorthwhile.text: Inspecting the collision and core fragments was unproductive: neither had an available operation, leaving the cooling step unclear.

surprise.text: I was surprised that the differentiated world needed to cool before a collision could expose its rocky layers; the earlier collision had already exposed its core.

arbitrary.text: The need to cool the asteroid before obtaining rocky fragments was physically understandable once revealed, but it was not obvious from the remaining goal.

continue.text: Yes. I would choose to continue to see how these different materials contribute to a growing Earth; the water–rock chemistry was particularly interesting.
